Title: Найбільший у минулому завод Чернігова визнали банкрутом

Summary: 
The Commercial Court of Chernihiv Oblast declared the state-owned enterprise 'Chernihiv Radio Equipment Plant' (ChEZRa) bankrupt on September 17, 2024, and opened a liquidation procedure. Founded in the 1960s, ChEZRa was once the largest employer in Chernihiv, with up to 10,000–12,000 workers in the 1970s–1980s, and operated under the Soviet Ministry of Radio Industry. It produced radar systems, missile and aircraft control units, and military and space electronics. After 2014, the plant lost most defense contracts and gradually ceased operations. Before bankruptcy, ChEZRa accumulated over 95 million UAH in debt, including 74.8 million UAH owed to the State Tax Service. The company had no assets sufficient to repay debts, and financial recovery without an investor was deemed impossible. Creditors voted for liquidation at a meeting on July 29, 2025. The liquidation means the company ceases to exist as a legal entity, and remaining assets will be sold to partially repay creditors. In recent years, ChEZRa produced electronic components for armored vehicles, supplied to Kyiv's 'Kuznya na Rybalskomu', Kyiv and Zhytomyr Armored Vehicle Plants, and Kharkiv Design Bureau for Mechanical Engineering. Russia was the main consumer of its products until 2014. The plant also had a civilian division, producing outdoor lighting fixtures. Production effectively stopped around 2019–2020; in August 2020, investor Anatoliy Dolesko stated that the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense had not signed new contracts for over a year, which 'finally halted production,' and that all assets were being sold 'at auction' to settle debts. At that time, the plant had 160,000 sq. m of industrial facilities with utilities. Former city mayor Vladyslav Atrushenko had planned an industrial park on the site. By 2025, inventory revealed only one RP-4 power distribution unit, five storage facilities, several old tractors and excavators, and a 0.23-hectare land plot. After production halted, the enterprise was reorganized into a new company: TOV 'Chezara Telemetry' (major beneficiary: Dolesko’s wife), established in January 2018, which manufactures electronic equipment. Chezara Telemetry reported revenue of 31 million UAH and a net profit of less than 1 million UAH in 2024, according to LIGA360.

Title: Суд завершит банкротство структуры челябинского правительства

Title: Oi (OIBR3) derrete até 28% com falência no radar; entenda o fator que 'segura' o fechamento das portas - Money Times

Summary: 
The shares of Oi (OIBR3) plummeted by up to 28% during the trading session on Wednesday, October 1, 2025, amid growing market concerns over the company's potential bankruptcy. The 7th Business Court of Rio de Janeiro issued a judicial decision that removed the current board of directors and paved the way for the company's liquidation. Judge Simone Gastesi Chevrand suspended Oi's extra-concursal obligations—debts incurred after the 2023 judicial recovery process—for 30 days. The decision also appointed judicial administrator Bruno Rezende to manage the company and Tatiana Binato to oversee the transition of essential public services. The court recognized Oi's critical role in providing telecommunications, including 70% of signals for CINDACTA (Integrated Air Defense and Air Traffic Control Center), which influenced the decision to delay full bankruptcy. The 30-day period allows Oi to transfer services to another operator and seek resources. According to bankruptcy expert Charles Hanna Nasrallah, the court's decision was a mixed one: it delayed liquidation to ensure continuity of essential services but may still lead to bankruptcy after the 30 days. Oi has over R$ 1.5 billion in extra-concursal debts. The company had previously sought a 60-day suspension of these debts in Brazil, arguing that without it, operations would be unviable. Oi's current cash reserves are R$ 21 million, insufficient to meet obligations beyond October 2025. If bankruptcy is declared, assets will be auctioned to pay creditors, though Oi may file appeals. The company also considered filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in the United States.

Published date: October 01 2025, 19:21
